correctness.rationale: Total domination is equivalent to meeting at least two parts. Two omitted vertices in one part have identical open-neighborhood traces, so at most one may be omitted. For omitted vertices from distinct parts \(i,j\), the traces are \(S\setminus V_i\) and \(S\setminus V_j\), equal exactly when both selected intersections with those parts are empty; under the one-omission rule this occurs exactly for two omitted singleton parts. This proves the three conditions, and the product polynomial with the two small support exceptions follows by independent choices in each part.

final_claim: For a connected complete multipartite graph, locating-total dominating sets are exactly those meeting at least two parts, omitting at most one vertex per part, and omitting at most one singleton part; the stated factored polynomial and minimum formulas follow.
limitations: All-set enumeration is claimed, but the classification is a direct definition-level consequence of complete multipartite traces.
